question.text: Which type of investor account can an NRI use to invest in mutual funds in India?

answer.text: Any overseas bank account with SWIFT facility

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that NRIs can invest in Indian mutual funds only through an NRE (Non-Resident External) or NRO (Non-Resident Ordinary) bank account. NRE accounts hold foreign earnings remitted to India, while NRO accounts hold Indian-origin income, and the choice between them affects how proceeds are treated. The Trap: Investments cannot be made directly from an overseas bank account; funds must be routed through an NRE or NRO account. Restricting the answer to only NRE or only NRO ignores the workbook's recognition of both as acceptable routes. Note: The source-supported rule is simple - either NRE or NRO. Treat any specific authorized-dealer-bank list or NRO repatriation cap (such as the often-quoted one-million-dollar-per-year figure) as items that need their own source before being quoted.
